Description:
Snagster captures your screen, lets you mark it up, records it and shares it. It is free and open source, works offline and needs no account.

Press Print Screen, then drag an area or click a window, button or menu. While you select, the part under the pointer lights up, so a single click takes exactly that window or panel. You can also capture the whole screen, a fixed size, a long scrolling page or fun shapes such as a circle or a star.

Mark it up with arrows, boxes, text, speech bubbles, numbered steps, colour emojis, a highlighter, a spotlight, a magnifier, blur and smart redaction for private details. Crop, cut out, add borders, shadows and torn edges.

Record videos (MP4 or WMV, up to 120 frames per second) with the computer's sound, your microphone or both. The graphics chip does the encoding where it can, so recording barely touches the processor or the battery. Record small GIFs, and make step-by-step guides as PDF, Word or web pages.

Studio mode is a live recording and streaming studio: build scenes from screens, windows, pictures and text, each with its own sound and a mixer, then record or go live on Twitch, YouTube, Kick, Facebook Live or your own server, on up to five services at once.

AI apps such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and VS Code can use Snagster through its built-in MCP server to capture, mark up, read text and record.

Snagster speaks 86 languages, picked automatically from your computer. Your pictures stay on your computer: no account, no ads, no tracking.
ShortDescription: Capture your screen, mark it up, record it and share it. Free, open source and offline, in 86 languages.
ReleaseNotes: First version in the Microsoft Store. The window is now drawn with Direct3D 12, so Snagster runs smoothly on company laptops and in Remote Desktop sessions.
